title: Terraform secure-egress-gateway module: layered SG/NACL, private DNS, and egress health checks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Private (VPC) customers require a hardened, auditable, and upgradeable Terraform module that centralizes outbound controls. Current deployments have ad-hoc SG and NACL settings across stacks which complicates upgrades, incident response, and auditability.

This ticket creates a new reusable module named secure-egress-gateway that implements a layered approach: strict default-deny security groups, defense-in-depth with optional stateless NACL rules for subnet-level egress enforcement, an integrated private DNS forwarding configuration for customer zones, and a lightweight health-check system to validate egress path availability (NAT gateway / proxy / egress firewall). The module must be safe to roll out to existing VPCs with a clear migration path and an automated test harness.

Goals:
- Provide a single Terraform module to manage egress controls consistently across private deployments.
- Support common enterprise patterns: deny-by-default, allow-lists for destinations, managed prefix-list integration, and optional egress-proxy routing.
- Emit telemetry-friendly tags/outputs for Console and billing (egress bucket tags, managed-prefix-list IDs).
- Include automated tests (terratest/Terraform validate), plan-time checks, and documented upgrade/migration guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for: allowed_destinations (CIDR/prefix-list IDs), egress_proxy_enabled (bool), private_dns_forwarders (list), allow_iam_tags and tag propagation.
Default behavior is deny-all egress; explicit allow list required to open outbound ports, with support for per-subnet overrides.
Optional NACL mode can be enabled to enforce stateless egress rules when required by customer compliance.
Module produces outputs: security_group_id, nacl_id (if enabled), managed_prefix_list_id (when created), private_dns_zone_forwarder_resource_id, and a health_check_arn (if health checks enabled).
Automated terratest suite validating: plan/apply/destroy in a non-prod account, health check runs that validate egress path to a set of test endpoints, and drift detection test.
Upgrade path documented and validated: instructions for migrating from ad-hoc SGs to the module without traffic interruption, including example 'apply -target' guidance and rollback steps.
CI pipeline blocks merges if terraform plan indicates any security_group changes that widen egress scope without an accompanying RFC link in the PR description.
Security review completed and signed off; relevant smoke tests added to monitoring so Console can show egress health per-customer VPC.
tasks: Design module interface (inputs/outputs) and write PRD - link to Confluence design doc
Implement core module: SG rules, optional NACL toggle, prefix-list integration, tagging and outputs
Implement private DNS forwarder resources and integration tests for conditional forwarding to customer zone or internal egress-proxy DNS
Add health-check Lambda (or use existing monitor) that probes egress path and writes results to CloudWatch/Datadog
Create Terratest integration tests and add to infra-ci pipeline
Write upgrade/migration playbook and run a dry-run migration in staging
Security review and threat model update; resolve review findings
Document module usage examples and add recipe to internal terraform-modules registry
tech_notes: Prefer managed prefix lists for large allow-lists to avoid 50-rule SG/NACL limits; module will optionally create/update a managed prefix list and accept external IDs.
NACL mode is stateless and evaluated at subnet level; recommend using NACL only where customers require subnet-level enforcement (e.g., regulated workloads).

Health checks should run from a small, dedicated VPC test instance or Lambda in the target VPC to validate NAT/proxy hop. Failures generate a Datadog event and a Console alert tied to the VPC resource tag.
Avoid welding provider alias complexity into module; accept provider config via inputs for cross-account deployments if needed but document caveats.
Plan to use Terraform 1.5 features and keep module backward compatible with existing root modules for 3 months before deprecation window.

Edge case: When migrating customers with pre-existing SGs that allow wide egress (0.0.0.0/0), module provides an opt-in 'audit-migrate' mode that keeps prior SG rules in place while we incrementally add tighter rules and run traffic/telemetry checks for 7 days before removal.
